newsitem.title: UK: ROYAL BANK SAYS STILL LOOKING FOR DEALS.
newsitem.headline: ROYAL BANK SAYS STILL LOOKING FOR DEALS.

text.p: The Royal Bank of Scotland Plc said on Wednesday its purchase of Birmingham Midshires Building Society did not satisfy its ambition to grow and it would still be interested in striking a larger deal.

"In no way does this mean we would not be interested in a larger transaction," Royal Bank's chief executive George Mathewson told a telephone news briefing. Mathewson said he was confident he could reduce the cost income ratio of the society.
"We believe with what they are doing and with what we can add to the business, that we will reduce the cost/income ratio as we move forward," he said.
Some rationalisation had already been announced with the society's closure of its Bracknell mortgage processing centre, this will mean 300 job cuts. The change will save around 8.0 million stg.
Mathewson said the cost/income ratio would be brought down to "competitive levels", which he said was in the region of 40 percent. Birmingham Midshires' ratio is currently in the mid 50s.
He said this could be achieved by increasing volumes and did not envisage closing any of the society's 115 branches or integrating any "in the foreseeable future".
"We believe we can get enough increase in volume, and we will get benefits from the utilisation of their expertise in mortgages to create the products".
But there would be "no meaningful job losses", Mathewson said, apart from those at Bracknell.
Mathewson said Royal Bank's corporate business had been growing very strongly and there was a need for balance by increasing its retail assets.
The bank's strategy, with its Direct Line insurance business and a joint venture with supermarket group Tesco Plc, was to increase its retail assets and customers, he added.
"We do not regard this as a deal which transforms the Royal Bank group. And we would be interested if the right deal comes along, in the deal that would (transform the group)," Mathewson said.
The Birmingham Midshires deal in no way satisfied all of his ambitions, he added.
Mathewson said Birmingham Midshires' chief executive Mike Jackson would be offered a board position, but he would not specify what this would be as talks would be going on over the next year.

Royal Bank does not anticipate any regulatory hurdles derailing the deal, which will bring its mortgage book up to 13 billion stg, of a total UK market of around 400 billion stg, around three percent of the market.
Mathewson said there would be synergies in both general and life insurance as well as in mortgage management "in the fullness of time".

Birmingham Midshires would end tied-agency agreements with Sun Life & Provincial Holdings Plc for life assurance, but would review general insurance arrangements as there were "business issues to be considered in the context".

Royal Bank said it had been able to buy Midshires for "a reasonable price". The deal was not dilutive to Royal Bank and could be earnings per share enhancing. "We are certain it is not going to be dilutive," Mathewson said.
